title: i'm a product dev, not a game dev. building a kingdom game with a team of AI agents, here's how it works (devlog #1)
author: lord007tn
selftext:
started hearthroad on 25 oct. it's an idle kingdom builder on one map, you link workshops dot to dot with roads and real carts carry every load. i don't write the code myself, here's the setup:

i write a brief, an agent (claude or codex) takes it in its own thread and branch and opens a PR. a few run at the same time, one on roads, one on the economy, one on art etc. i review and merge.

there's one design doc that's the rulebook. any PR that changes a rule or a number has to update the doc in the same PR, otherwise agents drift really fast and start inventing their own rules.

gates nobody gets to loosen. tests, perf budgets, a bot that plays the first hours on every PR. agents LOVE fixing a failing test by raising a timeout, that's banned. bots also play days of game time so i can balance without playing 10 hours myself.

the art (building cards, event scenes) is painted by an image model. the clip is the real game at 4x, nothing staged.

biggest lesson so far: the agents are fast, the slow part is me saying exactly what i want. vague brief = a very confident wrong PR. posting a devlog a day, happy to go deeper on any part of the setup if people are curious
